subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Unit 2 – Consolidation: Grammar, vocabulary and progress
outcomes: I can use can/could and have to/had to for now and the past.
I can make comparative adverbs like more carefully, better and worse.
I can use technology phrases like download an app and type a password.

tf.s: Could is the past form of can.
tf.why: I can swim now; I could swim when I was five.

tf.s: “People didn’t could send emails.” is correct.
tf.why: The correct sentence is: People couldn’t send emails.

tf.s: The comparative of badly is worse.
The comparative of well is weller.
tf.why: The comparative of well is better.

tf.s: “Didn’t have to” means it was not necessary in the past.
tf.why: They didn’t have to worry about Wi-Fi.

tf.s: We say “Jood have to remember lots of passwords.”
tf.why: With he/she we use has to: Jood has to …

tf.s: The comparative of quietly is more quietly.

tf.why: Turn off is the correct phrase for the TV.
We click on an icon and type a password.

tf.s: “You can type more fast than me.” is correct.
tf.why: We say faster than, not more fast.

boxes.q: Complete: Jood’s grandma ___ send emails to her friends.
boxes.why: In the past there were no emails, so she couldn’t.

boxes.q: Complete: Jood ___ remember lots of passwords!
Complete: Children ___ write with a pen or pencil – not a computer.
boxes.why: In the past it was necessary: had to.

boxes.q: Complete: They ___ worry about Wi-Fi working.
Complete: Anood does her homework ___ than Basma. (carefully)
Correct: “He speaks English more badly than his brother.”
boxes.why: The comparative of badly is worse.

mcq.q: Which is the correct form for the past?
mcq.why: Had to and didn’t have to talk about the past.

o: I have to use a password.
My grandfather didn’t have to use passwords.
Children had to write with a pen.

mcq.q: Correct: “My dad understands technology weller than my grandad.”
o: My dad understands technology better than my grandad.
My dad understands technology more well than my grandad.
My dad understands technology gooder than my grandad.
My dad understands technology best than my grandad.

mcq.q: With an old telephone, people ___ take photos.
mcq.why: Old telephones had no camera, so people couldn’t take photos with them.

mcq.q: Last week I couldn’t go online. I ___ finish my homework at my cousin’s house.
mcq.why: It was necessary in the past: had to.

o: She works more hardly than me.
She speaks more quietly than me.

mcq.q: “These days, children have to remember passwords. When Grandad was young, children ___.” Which ending fits?
mcq.why: In the past there were no passwords, so it wasn’t necessary.

mcq.q: Which pair shows then and now correctly?
o: Then: People couldn’t send emails. Now: We can send emails.
Then: People can send emails. Now: We couldn’t send emails.
Then: People has to send emails. Now: We had to send emails.
Then: People don’t send emails. Now: We didn’t send emails.
mcq.why: Couldn’t is past, can is present.
